solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Movie containing most unlikely material (7)

indicators.note: the movie word holds the next piece inside it

blocks.note: PIC is short for picture, a film
the last candidate is the least likely to be chosen

annotation.surface: A film is said to be full of the most improbable stuff.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Material' sits at the end looking like part of the film's contents; it is the definition, and plastic is a material.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: plastic is the man-made material moulded into bottles, toys and bank cards.

clue.text: Hot tap turns this way (4)

indicators.note: turning something round makes it run backwards

blocks.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hot, as on taps
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A plumbing note: the hot tap twists in this direction.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as instructions for turning a tap; in fact the whole of H plus TAP turns round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a path is a way in the literal sense, a track you walk along, and also a course of action.

clue.text: Moderate state argued on a regular basis (7)

indicators.note: take letters at a regular step: every other one

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly
the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of ArGuEd

annotation.surface: A middle-of-the-road politician's state keeps arguing its case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moderate state' looks like one phrase for a mild country; the definition is just 'Moderate'.
annotation.definitionFit: Average means ordinary or middling, as moderate does.

clue.text: Former partner avoiding more sex is characteristic (5)

indicators.note: keep away from, so leave those letters out

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner; these are the letters removed
extra means more
IT is old slang for sex (or sex appeal)

annotation.surface: Steering clear of further sex is typical of one's ex.
annotation.walkthrough: EXTRA plus IT makes EXTRAIT; the ex is avoided by dropping its opening EX.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a trait is a distinguishing feature of someone's character, a characteristic.

clue.text: Fanciful style captures timeless quality (8)

indicators.note: the style word holds the next piece inside it
without T, the abbreviation for time

blocks.note: chic is stylishness
merit is a good quality; losing its T leaves MERI

annotation.surface: A fanciful look manages to catch some enduring quality.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Timeless quality' reads as praise, but 'timeless' is an instruction to drop T from MERIT.
annotation.definitionFit: Chimeric means imaginary or fanciful, like a chimera.

clue.text: I’m surprised about backing a real outsider (2-5)

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: an exclamation of surprise
on means about, as in a book on birds
a as in 'fifty pence a go' means per

annotation.surface: Someone exclaims in surprise at people putting money on a rank outsider.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' suggests betting on a horse, which suits the outsider; here it reverses OH ON.
annotation.definitionFit: A no-hoper is someone or something with no chance, a real outsider in a race.

clue.text: Nod head at introduction to empress (6)

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: nut is slang for the head
used as it stands
first letter of empress

annotation.surface: A courtier bows his head as the empress is presented.
annotation.walkthrough: An uncommon word, built plainly from its parts once 'head' is read as NUT.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare technical word: nutate comes from Latin nutare, to nod, and describes a nodding motion of the head or a plant.

clue.text: Beehive possibly preserves constant location for feeding young (4,5)

indicators.note: keeps something safe inside it

blocks.note: a beehive is a tall, piled-up hairstyle: high hair
C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

annotation.surface: A beehive stores honey in one fixed place where its larvae are fed.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all bees and brood, but the beehive is the hairdo and the young are babies.
annotation.definitionFit: A high chair is where a baby sits to be fed.

clue.text: Pressure someone enduring wall-to-wall coverage? (7)

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure
one who lasts

annotation.surface: Someone is under constant media pressure, with coverage everywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wall-to-wall coverage' means saturation news; the question mark flags the literal reading, stuff spread over every wall.
annotation.definitionFit: Plaster is what covers a wall from one side to the other.

clue.text: Trooper is last in company to turn 18 (10)

indicators.note: take the final letter of the next word
turning the letters over rearranges them

blocks.note: used as they stand, for rearranging
last letter of company

annotation.surface: A young soldier turns eighteen, the last in his unit to come of age.
annotation.walkthrough: '18' looks like an age; it is a cross-reference to 18 down, ARCHIVE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an archive and a repository are both places where records or objects are stored for safekeeping.

clue.text: Head doctor’s article is, in part, absurd (9)

indicators.note: IS goes inside the other piece
made nonsense of, so rearranged

blocks.note: the definite article
PART rearranged; IS goes inside it
used as it stands

annotation.surface: A psychiatrist's paper is partly nonsense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In part' looks like 'partly'; it is IS placed in a jumbled PART. 'Head doctor' is slang for a psychiatrist or therapist.
annotation.definitionFit: Head doctor is informal for a psychiatrist, like shrink, and a therapist treats troubles of the mind.

clue.text: See doctor to check skin condition having left hospital (5)

indicators.note: to hold in check: the doctor holds the next piece inside
having left means having gone away, so the hospital's letter departs from the word

blocks.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
a rash; losing H leaves RAS
H is the map abbreviation for hospital; these are the letters removed

annotation.surface: A patient visits the GP to have a skin complaint looked at after discharge from hospital.
annotation.walkthrough: 'See doctor' reads as one medical instruction; 'See' alone is the definition, as in 'I see what you mean'.
annotation.definitionFit: See in its sense of understand, as in 'I see what you mean', which is what grasp means too.

clue.text: Gives legal validity to condition in each statute (13)

indicators.note: to condition something is to work it into a new shape

blocks.note: used as they stand, for rearranging

annotation.surface: A law is made valid by a condition written into every statute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Condition' reads as a noun, a clause in a law; it is a verb telling you to rework the letters that follow.
annotation.definitionFit: To authenticate a document is to confirm it as genuine and legally valid.

clue.text: Relationships restricting development of fiery young men (10)

indicators.note: the first word hems the next piece in
the letters develop into a new order

blocks.note: bonds are ties between people
FIERY rearranged

annotation.surface: Relationships hold back hot-headed lads from growing up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fiery young men' reads as one phrase; 'fiery' is the fodder and 'young men' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: boyfriends are typically young men, the male partners in romantic relationships.

clue.text: Prove sacked assistant spent more than necessary (8)

indicators.note: ransacked, turned upside down, so rearranged

blocks.note: PROVE rearranged
an aid is a helper

annotation.surface: Show that the fired assistant had been paid too much.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sacked' belongs with 'assistant' in the surface, a dismissed employee; it is actually rearranging PROVE.
annotation.definitionFit: Past tense matches past tense: having overpaid, you handed over more money than the bill required.

clue.text: Iron and gold boxes belonging to academic (9)

indicators.note: puts in a box, holding the next piece inside

blocks.note: to iron clothes is to press them
as in 'the house of my father'
OR is gold in heraldry

annotation.surface: An iron-and-gold strongbox that is the property of a scholar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Iron and gold' looks like the chemical symbols FE and AU; iron is the verb, to press clothes, and heraldic gold is OR.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a professor holds the top teaching rank at a university, so is an academic.

clue.text: Repeat what causes standards to deteriorate? (6)

blocks.note: par is the standard level
to rot is to decay

annotation.surface: Asking whether repetition is what makes standards slip.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'par rot', standards deteriorating; the question mark admits the stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words without thought, as a parrot mimics speech, so it means repeat.

clue.text: Noble argument against valuable item being returned (8)

indicators.note: sent back, so its letters run in reverse

blocks.note: as in pros and cons
an asset is something of value; reversed to TESSA

annotation.surface: An aristocrat objects to handing back a treasured possession.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Noble' could be an adjective; it is the noun, a titled person.
annotation.definitionFit: Contessa is the Italian title of a countess, a woman of noble rank, so the noun noble fits.

clue.text: Continue to signal large vessel (6)

indicators.note: attached to: ON is added to the end of FLAG

blocks.note: to flag is to signal
as in 'go on'

annotation.surface: A ship keeps signalling to a big vessel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Large vessel' suggests a ship at sea; it is a big jug.
annotation.definitionFit: A flagon is a big bottle or jug with a handle, holding wine or ale, and a vessel is any container for liquid.

clue.text: Author’s supporting chief source of historical information (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up means sitting underneath

blocks.note: arch means chief, as in arch-enemy
the author (the setter, I) has: I'VE

annotation.surface: A writer is backing the main source of historical facts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Author's' reads as possessive, but in crosswords the author is the setter, I, and the apostrophe S stands for has.
annotation.definitionFit: An archive holds original documents and records, which historians consult as primary sources.

clue.text: Sad individual is more sensitive about argument (8)

indicators.note: goes around the next piece

blocks.note: sorer means more tender
a row is a quarrel (rhymes with cow)

annotation.surface: A sad soul is extra touchy about a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: Row here rhymes with cow: a noisy quarrel. The container splits the comparative after its third letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A sorrower is someone who grieves.

clue.text: Irregular method to attract backing (7)

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters run in reverse

blocks.note: a way of doing something
to draw a crowd is to attract it; reversed to WARD

annotation.surface: An unorthodox approach to winning support.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backing' reads as support, the thing sought; it reverses DRAW.
annotation.definitionFit: Wayward means unpredictable and not following a set pattern, hence irregular.

clue.text: Youthful nurse put forward a proposal (6)

blocks.note: a third definition: one who tends, as in bartender

annotation.surface: A young nurse suggested an idea.
annotation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row: tender years, a tender who tends, and to tender an offer.
annotation.definitionFit: Tender means young, as in 'of tender years', and to tender is to offer formally.

clue.text: Half of brilliant people agree little by little (13)

indicators.note: keep only the first half of the word

blocks.note: INCREDIBLE, brilliant, cut to its first five letters
men as in people generally
figures that tally agree

annotation.surface: Half the bright sparks slowly come round to agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Brilliant' must first become INCREDIBLE before it can be halved.
annotation.definitionFit: Incrementally means by small steps, little by little.

clue.text: Cross and belligerent to some extent (5)

indicators.note: only part of the word is used

blocks.note: inside belLIGERent

annotation.surface: Someone is annoyed and somewhat combative.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, a synonym for belligerent; it is the noun, a hybrid animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A liger is a cross between a lion and a tigress.

clue.text: Present judge to auditor (4)

indicators.note: an auditor is a listener, so this is how it sounds

blocks.note: a judge hears a case

annotation.surface: Showing a judge's findings to an accountant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' suggests an accountant checking books; here it is one who listens.
annotation.definitionFit: Here means present, as when answering a roll call.

clue.text: Secures protection for digital assets? (5)

annotation.surface: A company locks down safeguards for its online holdings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Digital assets' sounds like cryptocurrency or files; the question mark flags the other sense, fingers and toes (digits).
annotation.definitionFit: To nail something is to fix it firmly, and nails protect the tips of fingers.

blocks.note: to nail something down is to fix it
fingernails shield the tips of the digits

clue.text: Model had style (9)

blocks.note: a design is a model or pattern
to have a meal is to eat it: had = ate

annotation.surface: A fashion model was stylish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Style' reads as a noun about fashion; it is the verb, to name or title.
annotation.definitionFit: To style someone is to call them by a title, and to designate is likewise to name or officially call.

clue.text: He takes coats from people attending in rotation (7)

indicators.note: rotating the word carries its last letter round to the front

blocks.note: people attending to a speaker are hearers

annotation.surface: A cloakroom attendant takes guests' coats in turn.
annotation.walkthrough: The coats are fleeces: the final S of HEARERS rotates to the front.
annotation.definitionFit: A shearer clips the fleece off sheep; the fleece is the animal's woolly coat, taken from it.

clue.text: Diminish what’s left of attention span (7)

indicators.note: the leftmost part of a word, its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of attention
to span a river is to bridge it

annotation.surface: Complaining that attention spans are shrinking.
annotation.walkthrough: 'What's left of' sounds like a remnant; in an across word, the left end is the first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: To abridge a book is to cut it down, so it diminishes in length.
